newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks maintain rise, for 11th session.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks maintain rise, for 11th session.

text.p: Caracas stocks rose for an 11th consecutive session to record heights on the belief of a sharp economic upturn this year in Venezuela, traders said.
The market's leading 19-share .IBC index finished up 0.60 percent, or 41.28 points, at 6,878.33 points, according to the exchange's preliminary figures.

As in recent days, the session saw large cross trades, in particular paints and packaging company Corimon B that accounted for nearly half the 58.4 million shares exchanged, worth 3.05 billion bolivars (US$6.41 million).
Among traded issues, 19 rose, 15 fell and 11 closed flat.
"The market was surprisingly fairly active with a good presence of local investors," a trader said.
Most traders expect the first quarter to be a good one for the Venezuelan economy, emerging from three years of recession. They noted inflation was receding, as the government predicted.
The Caracas bolsa had a record 1996, scoring the biggest increases on the International Finance Corporation (IFC) composite index of emerging market equities, with gains of nearly 115 percent.
Markets will be closed Monday for the Kings' Day holiday.
